title: Height-Balanced Invariant Preservation in an Online Two-Agent Single-Machine Scheduler
topic: An Optimal Online Algorithm for Single-machine Scheduling with Two Agents
author: Mateus Yonathan
journal: Polyglot Systems Lab Agentic Research Preprints

abstract: We study the online scheduling problem on a single processor with two agents that submit jobs sequentially. The objective is to minimize the makespan while preserving a strict height-balanced invariant on an auxiliary balanced search tree that indexes pending jobs. We propose a deterministic C implementation that maintains the invariant through local rotations and a priority-based dispatch rule. The algorithm achieves an asymptotic worst-case bound of $O(\log N)$ for insertion, deletion, and query operations, where $N$ is the number of pending jobs, and guarantees that the makespan equals the sum of all processing times. Formal invariants are proven using a structural induction on the tree, and static analysis confirms the absence of memory-leak and pointer-aliasing violations. The source code is publicly available at \url{https://github.com/myonathanlinkedin/c-lowlevel-systems/tree/main/algorithms/20261117_140135_an_optimal_online_algorithm_fo}.
